description: Application Performance Monitoring tools including New Relic, Datadog, Dynatrace, and APM best practices

questions.question: What is APM (Application Performance Monitoring) and how does it differ from traditional monitoring?
questions.answer: APM provides deep application-level insights beyond infrastructure metrics. Traditional monitoring: CPU, memory, disk. APM: request traces, code-level performance, database queries, external API calls, business transactions, user experience. Key features: 1) Distributed tracing - request flow across services, 2) Code-level profiling - slow methods identified, 3) Transaction tracking - end-to-end business flows, 4) Error tracking - exceptions with stack traces, 5) Database monitoring - slow queries, 6) Dependency mapping - service relationships. Example: New Relic shows payment transaction takes 800ms, breakdown: database query (600ms), external API (150ms), business logic (50ms). Identifies slow SQL query as bottleneck. Traditional monitoring shows CPU 40%, doesn't identify specific issue. APM tools: New Relic, Datadog, Dynatrace, AppDynamics, Elastic APM.

questions.question: How do you integrate Datadog APM with a Spring Boot application?
questions.answer:
Datadog APM uses Java agent for automatic instrumentation. Integration:

1) Add Datadog agent:
wget -O dd-java-agent.jar https://dtdg.co/latest-java-tracer

2) Run application with agent:
java -javaagent:dd-java-agent.jar \
  -Ddd.service=payment-service \
  -Ddd.env=production \
  -Ddd.version=1.2.0 \
  -Ddd.trace.analytics.enabled=true \
  -Ddd.logs.injection=true \
  -jar payment-service.jar

3) Docker integration:
FROM eclipse-temurin:17-jre
ADD https://dtdg.co/latest-java-tracer dd-java-agent.jar
COPY target/app.jar app.jar
ENV DD_SERVICE=payment-service
ENV DD_ENV=production
ENV DD_AGENT_HOST=datadog-agent
ENV DD_TRACE_SAMPLE_RATE=1.0
ENTRYPOINT java -javaagent:dd-java-agent.jar -jar app.jar

4) Kubernetes with Datadog agent:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: payment
        env:
        - name: DD_AGENT_HOST
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: status.hostIP
        - name: DD_SERVICE
          value: payment-service
        - name: DD_ENV
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: metadata.labels['tags.datadoghq.com/env']

5) Custom instrumentation:
@Service
public class PaymentService {
  @Trace(operationName = "payment.process", resourceName = "ProcessPayment")
  public Payment processPayment(PaymentRequest request) {
    Span span = GlobalTracer.get().activeSpan();
    if (span != null) {
      span.setTag("payment.amount", request.getAmount());
      span.setTag("payment.provider", request.getProvider());
    }
    return process(request);
  }
}

Datadog automatically captures: HTTP requests, database queries, Redis calls, Kafka messages, external HTTP calls. Visualize in Datadog UI: service map, flame graphs, trace search, error tracking.
